transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hi doctor. I guess… I’m here because I’ve been getting worried about something with my eating. It’s mostly late at night, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but once I start picking at food, I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” and then my hand just keeps going back.

It feels like, in that moment, I don’t really get to make the decision anymore. I know that probably sounds strange… but that’s the part that’s been bothering me.
Is this sense of not being able to control your eating limited to nighttime, or does it happen at other times of the day too?

Mostly at night, I think. I mean, that’s when I notice it and when it worries me. I’ll be just picking at something, and I’ll say to myself, “Okay, that’s enough, Santiago,” but then I keep reaching back anyway.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but in that moment it kind of feels like I’m not the one deciding anymore.
Does this feeling of not being in control happen with all types of food, or is it more with certain kinds of food, like snacks or things you might consider less healthy?

I guess I notice it more when I’m just picking at food late at night. I don’t know if it’s every type of food exactly… it’s more that once I start, I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” and then my hand still keeps going back.

It’s not like I want to make a big deal out of it, but that’s the part that worries me — like I’m not really the one making the decision right then.
Has there ever been a time during the day, not just at night, when you’ve felt like you couldn’t control your eating or stop yourself once you started?

During the day… not really, or at least I don’t notice it the same way. It’s mostly that late-night picking that worries me.

Like I’ll start eating something, and I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” and then my hand still goes back anyway. It’s not that I’m trying to ignore it exactly… it just feels like I don’t get to make the decision in that moment. I don’t know if that answers what you mean.
Has this experience of not feeling in control with your eating caused you any distress or affected your daily life in any way?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still going to my shipping and receiving shifts, and I’m taking care of what I need to take care of, so it’s not like everything is falling apart or anything.

But… I have started kind of avoiding being in the kitchen late with my family sometimes. Not because of them, really. I just get uneasy around the food, and I worry someone’s going to notice that I’m uncomfortable or acting strange. I don’t know if that counts as affecting daily life, but that’s probably the main thing.
Is this feeling of not being in control limited to certain types of food or situations, or does it happen regardless of what you're eating or where you are?

I think it’s more the situation than the exact food, if that makes sense. Like, it’s usually late at night when I’m picking at something, not so much where I am or what it is.

What worries me is that once I start, I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” and then my hand just keeps going back. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but in that moment it feels like I don’t really get to make the decision anymore.
Do you find yourself feeling especially concerned or upset about your body shape or weight?

I don’t think so… not especially. I mean, nobody loves getting older or seeing clothes fit different, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there really upset about my shape or weight.

It’s more… I get embarrassed about the eating part, I guess. But if you’re asking whether my body or weight is the main thing on my mind, I don’t think that’s it. Does that make sense?

Can you describe what happens during these late-night eating episodes? Do you feel like you’re eating a much larger amount of food than most people would in a similar period of time, and do you feel a lack of control throughout the whole episode?

Yeah… I mean, I guess it can be more than I want to admit. It’s not like I sit down with a plan to eat a huge meal or anything. Sometimes after work, I’m just standing in the kitchen, kind of telling myself I’m cleaning up leftovers.

But on some nights, I can go through several tamales, and then maybe a big bowl of pozole, tortillas… whatever rice or beans are left. Saying it out loud, yeah, that probably is more than most people would eat at that time.

And the control part… I wouldn’t say every single second, but once I get going, it’s hard to stop. I keep thinking, okay, that’s enough, and then I’m still reaching for more. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Do you feel distressed specifically about these late-night eating episodes, or do they interfere with your functioning in any way beyond avoiding the kitchen with your family?

I mean… distressed, yes, but I don’t want to make it sound like my whole life is falling apart. I’m still getting to my shipping and receiving shifts, and I’m handling what I need to handle.

It’s more at home, late at night. I’ve started kind of avoiding being in the kitchen with my family around then, because I don’t want them to notice how uncomfortable I get around the food. Or notice me acting weird, I guess. So it does affect me some, but I’m still functioning, if that’s the right way to put it.
